text:
Product relatedness is insufficient evidence of intent or compatibility. [TREC Product Recommendation](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html) distinguishes substitutes from complements; its [2025 annotation taxonomy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/trec-product-search/product-recommendation-2025/discussions/1/files) explicitly separates unknown compatibility from known incompatibility. Proposed diagnostic adaptation: construct training-prefix challenge sets for precise attribute matches versus broadly related items, explicit model/interface mismatches, and near-duplicate purchases. Store supporting title/description spans and label relation, compatibility, prerequisites, and satisfied demand separately. Missing ownership or compatibility evidence means “unknown”; historical purchases alone cannot establish that demand remains satisfied. Treat lexical duplicates as redundancy candidates, not confirmed unwanted recommendations.

For lightweight mining, use sparse word/character TF-IDF over available titles/descriptions and cosine similarity; these require no pretrained weights ([scikit-learn documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/feature_extraction.html)). Proposed implementation: retrieve lexical neighbors of training positives, then identify explicit attribute conflicts while retaining ambiguous neighbors as unlabeled. Research cautions against equating semantic proximity with negative relevance: [Hard-BPR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) modifies pairwise loss to reduce false-negative harm; [HNLMRec (2025, revised 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04726) identifies noisy semantic negatives and incorporates behavioral supervision, although its LLM approach falls outside the download constraint. Test a small mixture of random negatives and evidence-supported hard negatives, with confidence-weighted pairwise loss or Hard-BPR. Report slice coverage, unknown-label rates, and ranking violations as diagnostics; select changes only through the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Abstention applies to unsupported diagnostic judgments, while the host still receives complete recommendation rankings.
